problem: A company monitors incoming emails for spam. On average, $18$ out of every $150$ emails are spam messages. The emails are checked one by one until a spam email is found. Rounded to $3$ decimal places, the probability that a spam email is found before checking the $4$th email is{{field-1}}.

feedback.problem: A smartphone receives a software update that has a $60%$ chance of installing successfully on any given attempt. The phone keeps trying until the update installs successfully. Rounded to $2$ decimal places, the probability that the update installs successfully within the first $2$ attempts is{{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
A geometric random variable $X$ with probability of success $p$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=(1-p)^{x-1}p
$$

Let $X$ be the number of attempts until the update installs successfully. Since the chance that the update installs successfully on a single attempt is $60%,$ the number of attempts required to install the update can be modeled as a geometric random variable with a probability of success

$$
p=60%=\frac{60}{100}=0.6.
$$

So, $X∼\text{Geom}(0.6).$ In this case, $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =(1-0.6)^{x-1}(0.6) \\  & =(0.4)^{x-1}(0.6)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability that the update installs successfully in one of the first $2$ attempts is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 2) & =P(X\in {1,2}) \\  & =f(1)+f(2) \\  & =(0.4)^{1-1}(0.6)+(0.4)^{2-1}(0.6) \\  & =[1+(0.4)](0.6) \\  & =0.84.\end{aligned}
$$
